title: Model Explainability and Output Audit Rights Addendum
body:
Purpose
This addendum sets out the Vendor obligations and Customer audit and verification rights specific to model explainability, output traceability, and related evidence deliverables for any machine-learned models or model variants ("Models") supplied to or operated for the Customer by the Vendor as part of a Redwood Inference integration. It is intended to be appended to the Master Services Agreement or Data Processing Addendum where the Supplier provides inference or model-hosting services.

Scope and applicability
This addendum applies where: (a) the Vendor hosts, serves, or otherwise operates Models that process Customer data; or (b) the Vendor provides Model artifacts, training or evaluation artifacts, or inference endpoints on behalf of the Customer. It covers obligations for explainability artifacts, output and prompt logging, provenance metadata, and Customer audit rights described below.

Definitions (selected)
- "Explainability Artifacts": model cards, feature-importance reports, saliency maps, attention heatmaps, SHAP/LIME summaries, decision rules, or other materials that describe model behavior and drivers.
- "Provenance Metadata": immutable identifiers and provenance traces for model checkpoints, training datasets (or dataset manifests), preprocessing pipelines, dependency lists, CI build identifiers, and code-signature metadata.
- "Output Trace Logs": structured logs that link each inference result to (i) the model version and checkpoint identifier, (ii) the request identifier and timestamp, (iii) the prompt or input hash, and (iv) a minimal, reversible set of internal metadata required for debugging (e.g., tokenization boundary markers, sampling parameters).
- "Red-team Report": a summary of adversarial or safety testing performed against the Model including methodology, representative test cases, and mitigation steps taken.

Vendor deliverables and minimum standards
1) Model Card and Explainability Package. For each Model version deployed to serve Customer workloads the Vendor shall provide a Model Card in a machine-readable format and a human-readable summary. The Model Card must include: training data provenance (high-level), known limitations, intended use cases, typical failure modes, performance metrics across representative slices, and any pre- or post-processing applied.

2) Feature Importance and Sensitivity Reports. For classification or structured-output Models, the Vendor will provide feature-importance reports (e.g., SHAP summaries) for the top N features impacting decisions for the Customer’s primary workload (N to be agreed). For generative models the Vendor will provide representative saliency or attention-based analyses and an explanation of any sampling/settings that materially affect outputs.

3) Output Traceability Logs and Retention. The Vendor will retain Output Trace Logs for a mutually agreed retention period (default 90 days unless Customer requires longer for compliance). Logs must be exportable in JSONL or NDJSON format and contain the minimum fields enumerated in the Definitions section. Any user-identifiable content in logs will be handled in accordance with the Data Processing Addendum (redaction/hashing where required).

4) Provenance and Build Artifacts. For any Model checkpoint deployed for the Customer, the Vendor will maintain provenance metadata including: model checkpoint ID, training dataset manifest (high-level references acceptable where datasets are restricted), code commit hash, CI build ID, container image digest, and quantization/optimization pipeline identifier. Where artifacts are third-party or restricted, the Vendor will provide attestations and available metadata sufficing for reproducibility checks.

5) Safety and Red-team Evidence. The Vendor will produce a Red-team Report for Models with high-risk outputs or Customer-requested risk profiles. The report will include adversarial test sets, representative failures discovered, mitigation measures applied, and an assessment of residual risk.

Customer audit and verification rights
1) On-site or remote audits. The Customer may exercise audit rights (remote console access, secure export of logs, or limited on-site review) once per rolling 12-month period, or more frequently for material incidents. Audit modalities must respect the Vendor’s security posture; remote access will be via mutually agreed secure channels and view-only sessions where possible.

2) Evidence requests and SLAs. Upon request, the Vendor shall produce specified artifacts (Model Card, Output Trace Logs subset, provenance metadata, and Red-team summaries) within 15 business days. For high-priority incidents (security or privacy incident affecting Customer data), the Vendor shall produce a prioritized packet within 48 hours containing an incident summary and an actionable remediation plan.

3) Sampling for independent evaluation. The Customer may request sampling extracts of outputs (with PII redacted or hashed) for independent evaluation by Customer’s Security/Privacy teams or contracted auditors. The Vendor shall supply such samples within the timeframe above, with a cap on volume agreed in the contract to avoid operational impact.

4) Reproducibility checks. Subject to confidentiality restrictions, the Vendor will cooperate with Customer to the extent necessary to reproduce a reported misbehavior on a dedicated test harness using frozen inputs, model checkpoint, and deterministic configuration. Where direct reproduction is not feasible (e.g., proprietary third-party models), the Vendor will provide the closest available evidence and a written explanation of limitations.

Confidentiality and IP protection
- All artifacts provided under audit rights are Confidential Information. The Customer will use audited artifacts only for the purpose of compliance and operational verification and will not attempt to replicate or extract proprietary model weights or code beyond what is needed for the stated purpose. Reverse engineering of vendor proprietary models or distribution of checkpoint weights is expressly prohibited.

Security and operational constraints
- Secure channels and access controls. Exports and remote sessions will be performed over mutually agreed secure channels (TLS 1.2+, mTLS where supported) and under role-based access controls. The Vendor may apply reasonable controls to limit queries that could enable model extraction attacks during an audit.
- Rate-limiting and sampling. Audit requests shall be coordinated to avoid operational disruption; the Vendor may propose rate limits or time-boxed sessions if audit activities materially impact production traffic.

Remediations, dispute resolution, and escalation
- Remediation timeline. For verified high-severity findings (security, privacy, or safety vulnerabilities materially impacting Customer data or service), the Vendor will propose a remediation plan within 5 business days and implement mitigations according to an agreed schedule based on severity.
- Dispute resolution. Technical disagreements about reproducibility or root cause will be escalated to a joint technical committee (one technical lead from each party) for a 10-business-day review period. If unresolved, parties may engage an independent third-party technical reviewer (mutually agreed and cost-shared).

Limitations and carve-outs
- Third-party model constraints. Where the Vendor uses third-party closed-source models or managed services, the Vendor will provide the maximum feasible explainability and provenance evidence permitted by the model provider license. The Vendor’s inability to provide certain artifacts due to provider restrictions must be disclosed upfront as a non-conformance item.
- Data and privacy obligations. The Vendor’s obligations to supply logs or samples are subject to applicable data protection laws; redaction, pseudonymization, or hashing of personal data will be used where required and detailed in the DPA.

Operational examples and templates (appendix-style guidance)
- Model Card Template: short schema (Model name, version, trained-on, known biases, eval metrics by slice, last red-team date, contact).
- Export sample: JSONL schema for Output Trace Logs with example line demonstrating fields.
- Evidence Request Template: formal request language for audits, including scope, timeframe, and delivery channel.

Sign-off and integration notes
This addendum is intended as a practical bridge between legal contracting and technical verification. It can be attached to an MSA or SOW and tailored by filling the blanks for retention periods, sampling caps, and the frequency of independent audits. Parties should prioritize operational playbooks that map each contractual right to an API, UI flow, or support process before final signature.

Prepared by: Security & Compliance (Aisha Patel) — internal draft for legal review.

Questions / outstanding items (notes to negotiators)
- Agree default retention (90 days) vs customer-specific needs for regulated industries.
- Define the permitted scope of exported logs for third-party model providers.
- Set a maximum allowed sample volume per audit request to protect operations.
- Confirm independent reviewer selection process and cost-sharing approach.
